instructions: Rinse the rice and cook it according to the package.

Cut the fish into 2-inch chunks. Grate 1 tbsp of the ginger into a bowl, add the zest and juice of 1 lime, 1 tsp of the salt and the pepper, and toss the fish in it. Set it aside while you start the sauce.
Chop the onions as finely as you can. Mince the garlic and the rest of the ginger. Chop the tomatoes.

Heat the oil in a wide heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onions and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're soft and starting to turn golden. If they start to stick, add a splash of water.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute.
Add 2 tbsp of the berbere and stir for 1 minute, until the oil turns deep red and it smells toasty.
Add the tomatoes and 1/2 cup water. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it gets dry, until it's a thick, jammy sauce.

Add the fish and everything in its bowl, and spoon the sauce over it. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish flakes. Nudge the pieces gently with a spoon instead of stirring so they don't break up.
Take the pot off the heat and squeeze in the juice of the second lime.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lime.
Spoon a little of the sauce into a small bowl and stir in the remaining 1/2 tbsp berbere for anyone who wants more heat. Serve with the rice or with injera.
method_notes: No version I could read showed a rating, so this is a fallback lead: the Asa Wot (Berbere Spiced Fish Stew) page cooks onions down for a long time, adds ginger, garlic, tomatoes and berbere, and simmers lime-marinated fish in the sauce. Aisleprompt's version is a simpler skillet stew with crushed tomatoes. I followed the lead's order and cut the berbere to 2 tbsp in the pot (the lead uses 4 to 6) with the rest on the side so the base stays moderate.
